description: Cosmico is a team of engineering students from Kanjirappally building a 3D space tracker for Space Apps. We use NASA ephemeris and exoplanet datasets to calculate how fast you're really moving across Earth's spin, solar orbit, and galactic drift. From there, our tool applies the same math to filter movement noise out of telescope graphs for exoplanet hunting and calculate radio signal shifts for deep-space probes like Voyager 1.
summary:
Cosmico is an interactive 3D space-tracking web app 

It helps spot faint, distant objects like Planet X by stripping away the observer's own motion through space—accounting for six layers of movement from Earth’s rotation all the way up to the Cosmic Microwave Background. Users can inspect multi-epoch infrared sky data using blink-comparator and image-subtraction tools, filter out stellar noise with a Lomb-Scargle periodogram, and jump straight to five real astronomical benchmark targets like Barnard’s Star and WISE 0855.
details: Cosmico is a browser-based 3D space-tracking tool built for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Spotting faint objects in the outer solar system is hard because the observer is constantly moving through space and background stars flicker. Cosmico strips that noise away in three steps: 6-Layer Motion Subtraction: Models and removes observer movement across six reference frames—from Earth’s rotation and orbit up to Milky Way rotation and the Cosmic Microwave Background—using NASA ephemeris data and IAU coordinate transforms. Multi-Epoch Sky Viewer: Lets users compare sky scans over time using blink-comparator and image-subtraction tools to spot tiny shifts in position. Signal Filtering: Uses a Lomb-Scargle periodogram to separate real moving objects from flickering variable stars, tested against five benchmark targets (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis). Benefits & Intended Impact Cleaner Survey Data: Cuts down false positives when searching wide-field infrared surveys for distant objects like Planet X. Zero Setup: Runs completely in the browser with direct URL coordinate sharing, making quick visual checks accessible to students, citizen scientists, and researchers without heavy local software. Tools & Tech Stack Code & Hosting: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), hosted on GitHub Pages. 3D & Math: Three.js / WebGL for 3D visualization, custom matrix math for coordinate transforms, and a JavaScript Lomb-Scargle periodogram. Data: NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data and SIMBAD/VizieR astrometric catalog targets.
